correctness.rationale: The non-reset hitting-time Laplace transform follows from exact first-step backward equations on the actual graph. Two Chebyshev-type polynomial recurrences yield a rational formula for every integer clique size and path length; the standard exponential-restart identity yields the mean. For lengths at least three, positive coefficients of both derivatives establish strict increase at every nonnegative reset rate. Lengths one and two reduce to explicit monotone/strictly convex rational functions with exact minimizers. Independent full-generator rational Gaussian elimination agrees on 280 graph/rate combinations, with additional polynomial sign and finite optimizer checks; no infinite claim relies on experimental extrapolation.

evidence: Pal and Reuveni, arXiv:1607.06048, prove a general first-passage-under-restart renewal relation; the graph-specific optimization and phase boundary require the additional exact transform and positivity theorem.
Evans and Majumdar, arXiv:1102.2704, analyze resetting Brownian diffusion on a line, not this finite graph.

Riascos et al., arXiv:1910.13568, give network-resetting spectral formulas for degree-normalized random walks; Appendix B presents continuous-time dynamics with generator I-P rather than the unit-edge-rate combinatorial graph Laplacian here.
Förster et al., arXiv:2110.01946, give exact non-reset hitting-time reductions for necklace graph families, including cliques; no reset optimization appears in the relevant article sections.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal renewal identity subsumes the transformation from an arbitrary hitting-time transform to a restarted mean, but does not by itself state the all-length global optimizer. The new claim includes the transform and an independent polynomial sign argument for strict global monotonicity.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The strongest existing statements establish background modeling or universal renewal formulas. They do not appear to assert the strict nonbenefit of positive resetting for every length at least three under unit edge rates, nor the exact threshold and rate at length two. If another source gives an equivalent stronger parameterized formula, it would cover this claim and must take precedence; that remains a residual risk.

evidence: Zelenkovski et al. (2023), Random Walks on Networks with Centrality-Based Stochastic Resetting, describes lollipop topologies, but uses normalized discrete-time jumps and graph-averaged hitting times.
Riascos et al., arXiv:2110.15437, gives general discrete-time network reset models rather than unit-edge-rate continuous-time terminal-target optimization.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A common graph name or restart vocabulary does not make the statements equivalent: local holding rates and the fixed target differ, so no direct conversion preserving optimum is given in the inspected material. Exact all-size path-length threshold was not located; this is evidence-limited, not a uniqueness proof.

evidence: The 2023 lollipop figure examines a finite example with aggregated network observables, not a table of exact single-target optima for all clique/path sizes.
No exact matching endpoint-target continuous-time lollipop reset table was found in the inspected search results.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A numerical finite-example plot at different normalization does not tabulate or certify the analytic three-regime law. Absence from searched indexes does not establish historical uniqueness.

originality.rationale: General Poisson-reset renewal is explicitly prior. Full early source on continuous diffusion and the later first-passage restart paper provide the renewal method, not this graph-family global rate classification. The most closely related lollipop-network article studies discrete-time degree-normalized walks and all-target averaged first-passage statistics, rather than unit-rate-per-edge continuous time with a single terminal target. Thus its model-specific numerical results do not directly imply the all-clique-size three-regime phase boundary. Riascos et al. (2019/2020) include a continuous-time appendix with a generator induced from the degree-normalized transition matrix, still different from independent unit edge rates, and study rings, Cayley trees and random networks rather than this lollipop classification. Förster et al. (2021) derive non-reset mean first passage on necklace graphs but not restarted optimization. A further arbitrary-network reference also uses discrete time and supplies no corresponding closed lollipop theorem. Targeted source/alias and mathematical record searches found no direct coverage. Residual risk: an implicit specialization of an unindexed or unsurveyed general result.
residual_risks: An unindexed or incompletely read earlier general theorem might implicitly cover the all-size optimizer for exactly this process.
Related graph-resetting papers use time normalizations and observables that do not directly translate; an as-yet-unfound transformation could yield equivalent coverage.

value.rationale: The clique is a natural excursion trap and resetting trades avoidance of that trap against loss of progress along the pendant path. The exact result exposes a sharp, size-independent transition between a useful nontrivial restart optimizer for a two-edge path and strict harm for every path of three or more edges, plus an explicit optimal rate and large-clique saving. It classifies a physically interpretable first-passage design problem throughout an infinite two-parameter network family; it is not only a recurrence evaluation or a small enumeration.
